Project description
A small robot mouse with a camera which is rightfully terrified of cats. It patrols the room. When NVIDIA Cosmos Reason (cosmos3-nano-reasoner, served on CoreWeave GPUs) sees a cat in the live feed, the car panics: red lights, a 540 degree spin and a sprint away, with a panic clip on the dashboard. When Cosmos sees a hot dog, the car flashes green, and approaches.
Every 5-second clip the robot records goes into the event's VAST AI OS video pipeline, where DataEngine runs YOLO11, Cosmos captions and Cosmos-Embed1 into VastDB (756 clips so far). So the robot can answer plain-language questions about its own life: "when did the cat get closest, and did I get away?" comes back with an answer and the matching clips.
A Llama 3.3 70B planner on WandB Inference narrates what the robot is doing. Reflexes (steering, a 25 cm wall check, a disconnect watchdog) run on the laptop and never wait on the cloud; YOLO11 is the offline fallback detector.
For anyone with a pet camera, a security feed or a robot: video that can be searched and acted on instead of sitting unwatched.

hasPart.name: Technical architecture
hasPart.description: Camera (ESP32 MJPEG) -> laptop. Fast loop on the laptop: frame -> reflex policy -> drive commands over the Elegoo's 9600-baud link (change-only + 10 Hz keepalive), ultrasonic wall check, watchdog stops the car on stale video or lost link. Every ~3 s: frame -> NVIDIA Cosmos Reason (cosmos3-nano-reasoner on the event's CoreWeave GPU endpoint) -> JSON verdict: cat visible/side, open floor, boxed in, hot dog. Cosmos alone decides the panic; YOLO11 only when offline. Planner: Llama 3.3 70B on W&B Inference turns recent events + verdict into a narrated mode. Memory: recorder cuts 5 s clips -> relay on the event VM uploads to the VAST video pipeline (/api/v1/videos/upload with a cat-and-escape prom

hasPart.name: Setup instructions
hasPart.description: Hardware: Elegoo Smart Robot Car V4 with camera, a MacBook, a plush cat. python3 -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/pip install ultralytics opencv-python numpy torch transformers pillow openai requests fastapi uvicorn weave Simulator, no car: ./demo.sh then open http://localhost:8000 and click Start. Real car: join the car's ELEGOO Wi-Fi, run preflight.py (9-step first-hookup check), then ./run_car.sh. Event stack: COSMOS_BASE / COSMOS_MODEL from the team config, WANDB_API_KEY, and vm_relay.py running on the event VM for VAST. Tests: .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests

hasPart.name: Lessons learned
hasPart.description: Prompt wording decides the vision model's answer. Telling Cosmos the robot "must run away from a cat" made it say "cornered, cat approaching" on 15 of 15 frames, 11 with no cat. A neutral prompt that describes first, then answers, scored 10/12 on cat and 10/11 on cornered against hand-labelled frames. Let the big model confirm before acting: YOLO alone gave about 60 false panics on the real car; with Cosmos confirming, one real panic was confirmed and a false alarm rejected. A 9600-baud serial link is about 960 bytes a second, so the car only gets drive commands when they change, plus a keepalive. Keep the cloud out of the reflex loop: seconds of model latency are fine for judgement and memo
